plan.english: Be well, friend! Tell me, how many cows do you have? I have ten cows, and my father has a hundred cows. At dawn I milk them. Are your cows healthy? They are healthy, and the bull is big.

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: I have ten cows, and my father has a hundred cows.

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: They are healthy, and the bull is big.

plan.english: Friend, how are your sheep? They are well. In spring many lambs were born. How many lambs? Seven lambs. The lambs are dear to me. Does your daughter guard the sheep? She and the dog guard them.

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: In spring many lambs were born.

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: The lambs are dear to me.

plan.english: Tell me: are your horses swift? My horses are swift. I ride, and my son drives the swift horses. I want to see them! Come at dawn and see them!

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: I ride, and my son drives the swift horses.

plan.english: Do your dogs guard the sheep? They are awake by night and by day. My dog is not afraid. Does he kill wolves? Last year he killed a she-wolf. He is a dear dog!

clauses.english: Do your dogs guard the sheep?

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: They are awake by night and by day.

clauses.english: Last year he killed a she-wolf.

plan.english: Why are you upset, friend? My cow is gone. I am looking for it. Where did it go? I do not know. My dog is tracking it. Look! A cow is standing near the water. That is my cow! I praise the gods.

clauses.speaker: user
clauses.english: A cow is standing near the water.

plan.english: I saw a wolf by the road! Where did it go? My sheep are in that field! It ran in among the trees. Then I shall take the dogs and guard the sheep. Shall I carry the fire? Carry it! Wild beasts fear fire.

clauses.english: I saw a wolf by the road!

clauses.english: My sheep are in that field!

clauses.english: It ran in among the trees.

plan.english: What are you doing, friend? I am milking the cows. My daughter is milking the sheep. Do the cows love you? They love me. In the evening I sing to them. Sing to me! Sit down and listen!

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: My daughter is milking the sheep.

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: In the evening I sing to them.

plan.english: Where is your father? He is ploughing the field with the oxen. Is the earth dry? It is dry. It did not rain. May it rain soon! May Father Sky hear you!

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: He is ploughing the field with the oxen.

plan.english: What are you sowing in this field? I am sowing barley. My brother is sowing wheat. When does the barley grow? It grows in spring, and in the heat we cut it. Give me seed, friend! Take it! May it grow for you!

clauses.speaker: user
clauses.english: What are you sowing in this field?

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: It grows in spring, and in the heat we cut it.

plan.english: Did it rain yesterday? It rained in the night, and now the clouds are going away. Did it rain for you? It did not rain. The sun is warm, and I am thirsty. Drink water, friend!

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: It rained in the night, and now the clouds are going away.

clauses.speaker: user
clauses.english: The sun is warm, and I am thirsty.

plan.english: Is it snowing there? It is snowing. The cows are standing in the stall. In winter we sit near the fire. In my village it does not snow. Is your winter warm? It is warm. I want to see that winter!

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: The cows are standing in the stall.

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: In winter we sit near the fire.

clauses.speaker: user
clauses.english: In my village it does not snow.

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: I want to see that winter!

plan.english: Did you hear the wind in the night? I heard it. The wind was blowing, and the trees were trembling. The horses took fright. Are they afraid now? They are not afraid. The wind has gone away.

clauses.speaker: user
clauses.english: Did you hear the wind in the night?

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: The wind was blowing, and the trees were trembling.

plan.english: It is warm today, friend. It is warm indeed! I am sweating, and the sheep are lying under the pine. Where do the sheep drink? They drink at the spring. Its water is cold. Let us sit under the pine!

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: I am sweating, and the sheep are lying under the pine.

clauses.speaker: user
clauses.english: Let us sit under the pine!

plan.english: The frost is great today. The water has grown cold. Come to the fire, guest! Your fire is warm. Sit here and get warm! May the gods give you good things!

clauses.speaker: user
clauses.english: May the gods give you good things!

plan.english: Tell me, when does spring come? When the snow melts, spring comes, and the rivers swell. Then the cattle go to the fields. And in winter? In winter they lie in the stall, and we give the cattle grain.

clauses.speaker: user
clauses.english: Tell me, when does spring come?

plan.english: How shall I go through this river? Now the river is swelling. Do not swim! My boat is here; I shall carry you in it. And my horse? It will swim. Your horse will follow us.

clauses.speaker: user
clauses.english: How shall I go through this river?

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: My boat is here; I shall carry you in it.

plan.english: Why are you standing on the road? The wheel of my wagon broke. Shall I lift the wagon? Lift it! Then I shall put in a new wheel. Where are you going? I am going to my brother's village. We shall drink and sing.

clauses.english: Why are you standing on the road?

clauses.english: I am going to my brother's village.

plan.english: Where did you go yesterday? Yesterday I went to the sea with my father. Our two horses drew the wagon. What did you see? We saw the sea and many ships. I want to see the sea. Then come to us!

clauses.english: I want to see the sea.

plan.english: What is on that mountain? Snow lies on it in the heat and in winter. Pines grow there. Did you climb it? I climbed it with my brothers. Up above, we caught sight of the rivers and the fields. Did you not grow cold? We grew cold, and the sun warmed us.

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: Snow lies on it in the heat and in winter.

clauses.english: I climbed it with my brothers.

clauses.english: Up above, we caught sight of the rivers and the fields.

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: We grew cold, and the sun warmed us.

plan.english: Where are your pigs? They are among the trees. Are there wolves there? There are. Last year a she-wolf killed a piglet. Do not go there at night! At night I do not go. The dogs guard the pigs.

clauses.english: Last year a she-wolf killed a piglet.

clauses.speaker: user
clauses.english: Do not go there at night!

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: At night I do not go.

plan.english: Be well, man! Which path leads to the spring? This path leads to the spring. Go along it, then turn at the pine. Shall I arrive by evening? You will arrive by daylight. May the gods guard you on the road!

clauses.english: Where is the village of Fame-from-the-Gods?

clauses.speaker: user
clauses.english: I am a guest; I come from the mountains.

title: How to say: it is snowing

plan.english: Friend, how do I say this? It is snowing. It is snowing. Say it in winter! And how do I say this? The snow is melting. The snow is melting. When the sun is warm, say that!

clauses.english: Friend, how do I say this?

clauses.speaker: user

plan.english: How shall I say this? My dog is good. My dog is good. Say it to your dog, and he will rejoice. Dogs do not laugh! My dogs do laugh!

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: Say it to your dog, and he will rejoice.

plan.english: What is a foal? A foal is the offspring of a horse. It follows its mother. Do you have foals? I have three foals. Last year a new one was born. May it grow up and become swift!
